chunk_findings.detail: The stated invariant is that a phase reporting done holds zero open tasks, and a task becoming open under a done phase must re-open it (imported phases are supposed to refuse that instead). `_reopen_done_parent` is invoked from the `item.reopened` fold, then returns immediately when `parent.id in st.imported_done`, so it neither re-opens nor rejects. Seed an imported completion the same way the new test does (`item.completed` on `P9` with `imported: true` after `P9.T1` is done), then append `item.reopened` for `P9.T1`: the child folds to OPEN while `P9` stays DONE with its completion and gates intact — the same "done 18/19" inconsistency, and nothing in this change guards the reopen command the way `closed_phase_parent` guards task add.

chunk_findings.detail: `add_task` sets `refused=bool(closed_phase_parent(...))` for every `problem_of(draft) or missing_parent(...)` failure, not only the closed-phase reason. A draft that fails `problem_of` (bad id, empty title, or whatever that check returns) whose parent is a DONE phase in `st.imported_done` is returned as `Added(id, <validation text>, refused=True)`. Callers that treat `refused` as the operator-reopen policy (the same flag used for a taken id) mis-classify a malformed draft as a closed-phase refusal, and the closed-phase message is dropped because `problem_of` short-circuits first.

chunk_findings.detail: The helper claims a done phase re-opens only because it just gained an open task, but it never reads the child's state. On a restore or rework of a task that is still DONE (or otherwise not open) under a done phase, the fold sets the phase to OPEN, clears completed_at, gates, and lease, and drops imported_done. Given phase P done 2/2 and a re-add of completed child T (removed cleared, state still DONE), P becomes open with zero open tasks, so a phase that should stay done is invalidated.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/core/handlers/items.py:_reopen_done_parent

chunk_findings.detail: The stated fix is that both `task add` and `bug found --phase <done-phase>` must re-open a normally completed phase (and that an imported-closed phase must refuse the new open item). This suite only runs `task add` and a raw `item.reopened` append. A handler that reopens only on `task.added` still leaves the live inconsistency: phase P9 done, `bug found --phase P9` files an open bug, P9 stays DONE and reads done N/N+1, and this regression never fails.

chunk_findings.detail: `add_task` (and `task_add` via `_edge_refusal` / `missing_parent`) refuses every filing under an imported-done phase without looking at the draft's state or `readd`. `closed_phase_parent` is documented as applying only to a new open task, but it runs before `taken(..., readd=readd)` and ignores whether the child is still DONE. Given phase P in `imported_done` (state DONE) and a re-add of removed child T that is still DONE, `add_task` returns refused ("phase P is closed...") and never writes the event, so a completed task cannot be restored under a closed phase that would still have zero open tasks. The same call with an open draft is the intended refusal; a terminal draft is not.
